idea:
Consolidate the ensemble command surface around task-oriented top-level commands, delegating to the existing specialist workflows underneath:

- `ensemble-feature new <idea>` -- start the canonical feature lifecycle: PRD -> TRD -> validation/planning -> implementation, with the appropriate review and approval checkpoints. This becomes the front door and delegates to the existing resumable `ensemble-new-feature` workflow (the repo currently has both an older `ensemble-feature` pipeline and the newer resumable `new-feature` workflow -- consolidate to one canonical workflow underneath, with the other delegating during a compatibility period, rather than growing a third overlapping path).
- `ensemble-feature resume|status|abandon` -- manage the durable run (mirrors new-feature's existing resume/status semantics).
- `ensemble-issue fix <issue>` -- handle issue-driven investigation and repair, kept separate from feature work: a feature is usually planned from intent and artifacts; an issue starts from a reported problem and evidence. Add issue-specific actions as their semantics become clear.
- `ensemble-prd create|refine|...` and `ensemble-trd create|refine|validate|implement|...` -- retained as direct, document- or capability-oriented specialist tools for expert use and targeted work; never turned into a catch-all for every PRD/TRD operation.

Goal: give users an obvious front door (feature/issue as task-oriented commands) without taking away the composable specialist commands (PRD/TRD). Constraints: pick one canonical workflow name (not two synonymous "new" entry points indefinitely); keep ensemble-feature scoped to feature lifecycle only; keep issue work and feature work as distinct workflows even though their implementation stages overlap; name subcommands after their actual operation once behavior is settled (e.g. avoid an ambiguous "re-create" that could mean recreating an issue record, regenerating a plan, or retrying a failed fix).
